tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

1	# Kitty: shared trip-cost tracker — design
2	
3	Date: 2026-11-17
4	Status: draft for approval
5	
6	## Intent and why
7	
8	A group of friends on a trip need to record who paid for what, so that at
9	the end they know who owes whom and how to even up with as few paybacks as
10	possible. The owner is not a programmer; their friend Sam writes scripts
11	and will hook the tool up to a spreadsheet. So the tool is a command-line
12	program whose reports are machine-readable JSON in exactly the format
13	below, and which never crashes on bad input: it explains the problem and
14	stops.
15	
16	## Goals
17	
18	- Track members, expenses (with flexible splits and foreign currencies),
19	  payments between members, and exchange rates.
20	- Report balances, a settlement plan, per-person history, a per-category
21	  spending report, and a CSV export.
22	- Exact money math: shares of an expense always add up to it to the cent.
23	
24	## Non-goals
25	
26	- No GUI, no web, no multi-user sync, no editing of an existing expense
27	  (remove and re-add instead), no automatic exchange-rate lookup.
28	
29	## Anti-goals (would be a failure even if it "works")
30	
31	- Needs anything installed beyond the Mac's Python 3.9.6.
32	- A refused command changes `kitty.json` in any way, or a crash leaves it
33	  half-written.
34	- A Python traceback shown to the user for bad input.
35	- Balances that drift by a cent, or shares that don't sum to the expense.
36	- Past expenses silently changing when the group or a rate changes.
37	
38	## Constraints
39	
40	- Run as `python3 -m kitty <command> ...` from the folder that contains the
41	  `kitty` package. Python 3.9.6, standard library only (so no `match`, no
42	  `X | Y` type unions at runtime, `date.fromisoformat` is limited, etc.).
43	- State lives in `kitty.json` in the **current working directory**.
44	- Success: exit status 0. Any refusal: one line `error: <message>` on
45	  stderr, nothing on stdout, exit status 1, `kitty.json` byte-for-byte
46	  unchanged. This includes command-line usage mistakes (unknown command,
47	  missing argument, unknown option) — argparse's default exit status 2 must
48	  be overridden to 1 with the same `error:` format.
49	
50	## Approaches considered
51	
52	1. **Plain Python package, stdlib only, JSON file state** — chosen.
53	   `decimal` for money, `json`, `csv`, `argparse`. Matches every constraint.
54	2. **SQLite database for state** — rejected: Sam asked for `kitty.json`, and
55	   a plain JSON file is easier for his scripts.
56	3. **Third-party libraries (e.g. click, a money library) or another
57	   language** — rejected: violates "nothing to install" and
58	   `python3 -m kitty`.
59	
60	The owner agreed to approach 1.
61	
62	## Commands and output
63	
64	All JSON output is printed with Python's default `json.dumps` separators
65	(`", "` and `": "`), on one line, as in the examples. Money is always a
66	string with exactly two decimals. Money is in the main (base) currency,
67	except an expense's own `amount`. Object key order is significant and is
68	given below.
69	
70	| Command | Prints on success |
71	|---|---|
72	| `init CUR` | nothing |
73	| `member add NAME` / `member remove NAME` | nothing |
74	| `member list` | `["Alice", "Bob"]` — join order |
75	| `expense add PAYER AMOUNT DESCRIPTION [opts]` | the new ID, e.g. `1` |
76	| `expense list` | list of expense objects, by ID |
77	| `expense remove ID` | nothing |
78	| `payment add FROM TO AMOUNT [--currency C] [--date D]` | nothing |
79	| `rate set CUR RATE` | nothing |
80	| `balances` | object, members in join order |
81	| `settle` | list of payments, in the order computed |
82	| `history NAME` | list of entries |
83	| `report` | object of objects |
84	| `export FILE` | nothing (writes the CSV) |
85	
86	Examples (from Sam):
87	
88	- `expense list`: `[{"id": 1, "date": "2026-07-14", "payer": "Alice", "description": "Dinner", "amount": "45.00", "currency": "USD", "base_amount": "41.40", "category": "food", "shares": {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "20.70"}}]`
89	- `balances`: `{"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "-20.70"}`
90	- `settle`: `[{"from": "Bob", "to": "Alice", "amount": "20.70"}]`
91	- `history Bob`: `[{"date": "2026-07-14", "description": "Dinner", "change": "-20.70", "balance": "-20.70"}]`
92	- `report`: `{"food": {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "20.70"}}`
93	
94	Empty results print `[]` or `{}`.
95	
96	## Rules decided with the owner
97	
98	### Kitty and state
99	- `init CUR` creates `kitty.json` with CUR as the main currency. Refused if
100	  `kitty.json` already exists. Every other command is refused if it doesn't.
101	- Anything that changes state is fully validated first; the file is saved
102	  only on success, by writing a temp file in the same folder and
103	  `os.replace`-ing it over `kitty.json`.
104	
105	### Members
106	- Names are case-insensitive for matching everywhere (in every command and
107	  option), but always displayed as first added. Adding a name that matches
108	  an existing one case-insensitively is refused.
109	- Names may not contain `,` or `=`. (Builder's call: also refuse empty or
110	  all-whitespace names; strip surrounding whitespace.)
111	- `member remove` is refused if the person appears in any expense (as payer
112	  or in its shares) or any payment (as sender or receiver). Otherwise it
113	  succeeds. Unknown name is refused.
114	
115	### Expenses
116	- PAYER must be a member. The payer need not be among the people sharing.
117	- "Everyone" (no split option) means the members at the moment the expense
118	  is added; the computed shares are stored with the expense and never
119	  recomputed. Later joiners are not included in earlier expenses.
120	- At most one of `--among`, `--exact`, `--shares`, `--percent`.
121	- `--among A,B`: equal split among those named.
122	- `--exact A=30,B=20`: amounts in the expense's own currency; must add up
123	  to AMOUNT exactly.
124	- `--shares A=2,B=1`: split in proportion.
125	- `--percent A=60,B=40`: must add up to exactly 100.
126	- Every name in a split must be a member; duplicates are refused.
127	- `--currency` defaults to the main currency. Any other currency must have
128	  a rate set, else refused.
129	- `--date YYYY-MM-DD` must be a real calendar date in exactly that format;
130	  default is today's local date.
131	- `--category` defaults to `other`.
132	- IDs start at 1, increase by 1, and are never reused after removal.
133	  `expense remove` of an unknown ID is refused.
134	
135	### Amounts
136	- AMOUNT (expenses, payments, `--exact` values) must be a positive number
137	  with at most two decimals. `12.345` is refused, not rounded. Zero,
138	  negative, and non-numbers are refused.
139	
140	### Currency and rates
141	- `rate set USD 0.92`: one USD = 0.92 main currency. Rate must be a
142	  positive number. Setting a rate for the main currency is refused.
143	- An expense or payment is converted with the rate in force when it is
144	  added; that rate is frozen with it. Later `rate set` affects only things
145	  added afterwards.
146	- `base_amount = amount × rate`, rounded to the cent with halves always
147	  going up (0.125 → 0.13).
148	
149	### Splitting and cents
150	- Each person's exact part of `base_amount` is computed, rounded **down** to
151	  the cent, then the leftover cents go out one each, in order, until none
152	  remain. Order is the order typed in the option, or join order for
153	  "everyone".
154	  - 10.00 among Alice, Bob, Cara → 3.34, 3.33, 3.33.
155	  - 10.00 with `--shares A=1,B=2` → A 3.34, B 6.66.
156	- Percent and shares work the same way (exact proportional part, round
157	  down, leftover cents in listed order).
158	
159	### Payments
160	- FROM and TO must be members and must differ. Same amount, currency, date
161	  rules as expenses.
162	
163	### Balances
164	- balance = (sum of `base_amount` of expenses they paid) − (sum of their

173	  ignoring case. Payments listed in the order worked out. Nothing to settle

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.
